successors.name: Shu
successors.text: the Chengdu Plain, where Shu appears in 1046

ledger.x: c. 1700 BC: the Sanxingdui culture on the Chengdu Plain. Infobox 'Dates: c. 1700 - c. 1150 BC'; Period I belongs to the Baodun culture and Periods II-III are the Sanxingdui culture, 'contemporaneous with the Shang dynasty'. Region is the researcher's reading of 'Chengdu Plain'.
c. 1600 BC: a walled city is founded at Sanxingdui. 'Archaeological digs at the site showed evidence of a walled city founded c. 1,600 BCE'; a trapezoid of about 3.6 km2 with walls 8-10 m high.

c. 1150 BC: the Sanxingdui culture ends. The infobox ends it c. 1150 BC; the page dates no cause (flood, earthquake or invasion are suggested) and Jinsha, 40 km away, 'is thought to be the relocated capital of the Shu kingdom' (Jinsha page: Shi'erqiao culture 1200-800 BC).

certainty.note: An archaeological distribution, never a boundary; soft throughout.
